summary: Notion explicitly lets you start OAuth authorization as soon as the integration's credentials and redirect URI are configured; Marketplace submission or review is not required. The main choice is installation scope, which cannot be changed later.

approval.typical_timeline: Minutes. You can start the OAuth flow immediately after creating the integration.
approval.notes: Listing in Notion's Marketplace is optional and managed separately through the Listings section.

steps.title: Create an OAuth integration in the Developer portal
steps.detail: New OAuth integration: fill in connection details, set redirect URI(s) under OAuth configuration, and choose the installation scope.

steps.title: Choose installation scope carefully
steps.detail: Either Any workspace (public integration) or a specific set of workspaces (scoped integration). This cannot be changed after creation.

steps.title: Get the authorization URL and credentials
steps.detail: The Configuration tab provides the authorization URL, client ID and secret. Keep secrets out of source control.

steps.title: Send users through the authorization prompt
steps.detail: Users see your connection's capabilities, pick pages/databases in a page picker, and Notion redirects back to your redirect URI with a code.

steps.title: Exchange the code for an access token
steps.detail: POST the temporary code to Notion's token endpoint; store the returned access token for future API calls.

nuances: The page picker only shows pages the user has full access to, and if the user abandons the flow after Allow access, the connection gets nothing.
You can attach a public Notion page as an optional template that users duplicate during the auth flow.
For workspace-internal automation, internal connections (static token, manual page sharing) or personal access tokens may fit better than OAuth.
Notion also requires a Notion-Version header on API requests when not using their SDK.
agent_can_do: Advise OAuth integration vs internal connection vs PAT for your use case
Generate the authorization link and token-exchange code
Explain the page-picker consent model to your users
human_must_do: Create the integration in your workspace's Developer portal
Keep client credentials out of the repo
